## Introduction

The purpose of this document is to define the handoff process for the Medi-Cal build team to transition monitoring, tasks, or support of an application to the Operational support team. Please note that any type of request needs to be submitted prior to the “go live” date or turnover to operations whenever possible. This document outlines the process used, ensuring consistency and turnover to the operations team.

# AFLPA User Access

BusOps operational staff that require access to the AFLPA web application for their job duties will have to create a CA-MMIS ServiceNow access request ticket requesting access to the AFLPA web application.

Open a CA-MMIS ServiceNow access request ticket by accessing the CA-MMIS Service Portal ([Service Portal – Service Portal (servicenowservices.com)](https://dcammis.servicenowservices.com/sp?sysparm_stack=no) to create a Service Now request ticket under ‘BusOps Services (Gainwell) for access to the AFLPA application.

# AFLPA Web Application Information

This section is an overview of aspects of the AFLPA web application that will assist BusOps operations in use of the AFLPA system. The AFLPA system receives inputs from various sources or other systems. When AFLPA loads input from another source or system AFLPA creates a job and assigns a JobID to the job. Each JobID is unique and allows the job (or correspondence letter package) to be tracked through the AFLPA system.

For further detail regarding the AFLPA Web Application, please refer to the *AFLPA SOP* in the MCSP library.

page_texts.11:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-1-data-files-are-missing-from-the-aflpa-inbound-folders-not-present-after-they-are-scheduled-to-be-placed-there-by-the-managed-file-transfer-mft-team]

#### **Scenario 1:** Data files are missing from the AFLPA inbound folders, not present after they are scheduled to be placed there by the Managed File Transfer (MFT) team.

This problem can be detected by:

* Expected data not appearing in the AFLPA.
* Receiving a SNOW ticket from the MFT team that files are missing.
* The AFLPA system sends a job error email (via SMTP) to the AFLPA support team’s email mailbox:  Aflpa@gainwelltechnologies.com

To solve the problem:

1. The AFLPA support team determines if the files are missing by examining the inbound folders on the application server’s D:\...Inbound folders and the D:\...MOVEitAutomationLogs, or if the files are present but there is a job failure.
2. If the files are missing, the AFLPA support team opens a SNOW ticket with the MFT team.
3. The MFT team will trace the missing file problem and collect the missing files.
4. After the files are present, the AFLPA support team ensures the files are loaded into the DB either by waiting for the next scheduled job cycle (if timing allows this) or scheduling an off-cycle job.
5. After validating the data loaded properly into the DB, the ticket is marked as resolved.
page_texts.12:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-2-when-files-already-exist-in-the-aflpa-inbound-folder-but-data-is-unexpectedly-not-present-in-the-aflpa-db]

#### **Scenario 2:** When files already exist in the AFLPA inbound folder, but data is unexpectedly not present in the AFLPA DB.

This problem can be detected by:

* Expected data not appearing in the AFLPA DB.
* Receiving a SNOW ticket from a user that data is missing.
* The AFLPA system has sent a job error email (via SMTP) to the AFLPA support team’s email mailbox:  Aflpa@gainwelltechnologies.com

To solve this problem:

1. The AFLPA support team determines if the files are missing by examining the inbound folders on the application server’s D:\...Inbound folders and the D:\...MOVEitAutomationLogs, or if the files are present but there is a job failure.
2. If the files are present, the AFLPA support team opens a SNOW ticket assigned to the AFLPA support team.
3. The AFLPA support team ensures the SSIS applications, SQL server and Web App services are operational. If services have stopped, the AFLPA support team restarts the offending service.
4. The AFLPA support team analyses the AFLPA SSISDB/MSDB tables to see how and where the job failed and what data may remain to be loaded if a failure occurred mid-stream.
5. The AFLPA support team may ask the leveraged DBA team for assistance, if needed.
6. In the rare chance a failure resulted in a partial data load, the AFLPA support team will write a custom script to make a backup copy of the partially loaded tables and delete the improperly loaded data from the original tables.
7. The AFLPA support team will then run an off-cycle job.
8. After validating the data loaded properly into the DB, the ticket is marked as resolved.
9. The custom script and backup table are noted for later removal as an extra cleanup step in a future planned deployment.
page_texts.13:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-3-missing-data-is-caused-by-an-incoming-file-transfer-failure-that-occurs-due-to-network-connectivity-mft-information-technology-it-system-failure-application-connectivity-db-connectivity-or-any-other-infrastructure-issue]

#### Scenario 3: Missing data is caused by an incoming file transfer failure that occurs due to network connectivity, MFT Information Technology (IT) System failure, application connectivity, DB connectivity, or any other infrastructure issue.

This problem can be detected by:

* Expected data not appearing in the AFLPA DB Web App UI.
* Receiving a SNOW ticket from the leveraged support team(s).
* The AFLPA system sends a job error email to the AFLPA support team’s email mailbox:  Aflpa@gainwelltechnologies.com

To solve this problem:

1. AFLPA support team will evaluate if the failed service is still causing a problem. This may require opening SNOW tickets with the Infrastructure DBA and ODC (Orlando Data Center) Level 1 support teams.
2. The AFLPA support team determines if the files are missing by examining the inbound folders on the application server’s D:\...Inbound folders and the D:\...MOVEitAutomationLogs, or if the files are present but there is a job failure.
3. If the files are missing, the AFLPA support team opens a SNOW ticket with the MFT team.
4. The MFT team will trace the missing file problem and provide the files as originally intended.
5. After the files are present, the AFLPA support team ensures the files are loaded into the DB either by waiting for the next scheduled job cycle (if timing allows this) or scheduling an off-cycle job.
6. Further, the AFLPA support team will evaluate if the failure resulted in a partial data load. If this unlikely event occurred, the AFLPA support team will write a custom script to make a backup copy of the partially loaded tables and delete the improperly loaded data from the original tables.
7. The AFLPA support team will then run an off-cycle job.
8. After validating the data loaded properly into the DB, the ticket is marked as resolved
page_texts.14:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-4-a-user-can-access-the-web-ui-portal-but-the-users-screen-for-selected-job-manager-does-not-run-at-all-or-is-missing-data]

#### Scenario 4: A user can access the Web UI portal, but the user’s screen for selected job manager does not run at all or is missing data.

This problem can be detected by:

* Expected data not appearing in the AFLPA DB and Web App UI
* Receiving a SNOW ticket from an end-user.
* Notification by a leveraged team that a service is halted.

To solve this problem:

1. AFLPA or the end user runs the user interface to evaluate whether the problem is data-related, a user interface error, or an environment problem.
2. If the problem is data-related, and the user understands where the upstream data issue occurs, he/she will enter a SNOW ticket to the proper team.
3. If the problem is data-related and the user does not know the problem, the AFLPA will pursue steps listed in Scenarios 1-3 above.
4. If the problem is an error within the user interface, the AFLPA team will troubleshoot the interface.
   * 1. If the issue is with the user interface, the AFLPA technical support team will provide user interface troubleshooting to resolve the issue.
     2. If the problem is with the data, the AFLPA technical support team will troubleshoot to identify whether the problem is with the design itself or with the upstream data.
        + 1. If the problem is within the user interface design, the development environment is first updated, and then changes are deployed to the production environment. Any changes to the code must be posted to the ADO and acquire proper change authorization.
          2. If the problem is data-related the AFLPA Operator will contact the AFLPA system administrator and /or DBA responsible for the data, and (as appropriate) reassign the SNOW ticket.
5. If the problem is an environment-related issue within the AFLPA system, the AFLPA technical support team will check all services are running. The team may choose to “restart” the Web App portal and or SQL server. This will be postponed until after-hours, if possible.
6. If the problem is an environment-related issue with the server, network, or other upstream service, the AFLPA technical support team will follow steps in Scenario 3.
7. After resolution of the issue, the AFLPA technical support team updates the incident ticket and change status to resolved
page_texts.15:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-5-a-user-cannot-access-the-web-app-ui-portal]

#### Scenario 5: A user cannot access the Web App UI portal.

This problem can be detected by:

* Receiving a SNOW ticket from an end-user that the user’s previously operational process is now not working.
* Receiving an error page while trying to access the Web App UI indicating that the Web App UI portal service is not available.
* Receiving a notification from the leveraged DBA or system administration teams that the Web APP UI portal service is down.

To solve this problem:

1. The AFLPA technical support team will first check to see that the Web App UI portal is operational and running properly.
2. If the portal is down for all users, the AFLPA technical support team will restart the Web App UI in IIS. If this does not solve the problem or the service will not start, the AFLPA technical support team will engage the Infrastructure DBA and ODC Level 1 support teams.
3. If the portal is operational for all users except the sole affected user who submitted the SNOW incident, the AFLPA technical support team will check the following
   * + user’s account is properly defined in the application database.
     + User’s account is assigned to the proper Medi-Cal AD group
     + These steps will likely resolve the issue, and the AFLPA technical support team marks the incident ticket Resolved.
page_texts.16:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-6-low-disk-space-in-aflpa-application-server]

#### Scenario 6: Low disk space in AFLPA application server.

This problem can be detected by:

* Infrastructure ODC Level 1 support team or leveraged DBA contacts the AFLPA technical support team about a disk space problem.
* The AFLPA technical support team notices data file missing problems. This indicates not enough space exists for newly arriving data files.
* Users report (via SNOW tickets) or AFLPA support team notices strange performance or slow performance issues, which are typically memory or space related.

To solve this problem:

1. The AFLPA support team opens a SNOW incident, if one is not opened already.
2. The AFLPA support team member logs into the AFLPA server and frees up the disk space by deleting older archived files from the D:\...Inbound\Archive folders.
3. The AFLPA support team will assess if the space freed is adequate to eliminate job failures.
4. If the problem persists, the AFLPA support team will transfer the SNOW ticket to the ODC Level 1 support team to address the issue at the server and Database.
5. The Infrastructure ODC Level 1 support team will add new disk space, either as a SEV 1 issue if other job failures are imminent, or a SEV 3 if freeing up space removed the low disk space concern.
6. The AFLPA support team will examine for potential data losses, as outlined in Scenarios 1-3 above.
7. After resolution of the issue, the AFLPA support team marks the incident ticket Resolved.
page_texts.17:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-7-complete-environment-failure-or-failure-of-the-odc-requiring-a-full-restore-onsite-or-offsite]

#### Scenario 7: Complete environment failure, or failure of the ODC requiring a full restore onsite or offsite.

This problem can be detected by:

* Infrastructure ODC Level 1 support team notification.
* The AFLPA support team notices complete system unavailability of all services.

To solve this problem:

1. The AFLPA support team opens a SNOW incident ticket if one is not opened already.
2. The Infrastructure ODC Level 1 support team troubleshoots the environment/server issues, up to and including the complete rebuild of standard servers.
3. Once a stable environment is ready with both a DB and application server, the DBA team will install SQL Server and the AFLPA support team will install Web App UI.
4. The AFLPA support team will rebuild the non-standard software (SW) and configurations according to the variables and settings outlines in the *SDP\_AFLPA\_Appendix\_N\_Configuration Guides.docx* document.
5. The AFLPA support team will restart all services.
6. The AFLPA support team will evaluate missing file and data issues and resolve them as described in Scenarios 1-3.

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#scenario-8-data-gateway-is-not-working-or-api-calls-are-not-receiving-a-response]

#### Scenario 8: Data Gateway is not working, or API calls are not receiving a response

This problem can be detected by:

* Receiving a SNOW ticket from an end-user that the API calls are not working.
* Receiving a notification from the system that the Data Gateway is down.
* Receiving a notification from the leveraged DBA or system administration teams that the SQL server is down.

To solve this problem:

1. If the data gateway is unreachable restart the gateway and try again.
2. Unable to connect – Invalid connections credentials. Verify that you have the correct username and password
3. Unable to connect –Cannot connect to the database. Verify the name of the database and that the user credential has the proper permissions to access the database
4. Unable to connect- unknown error in the data gateway. Validate that you can access the machine that is hosting the data gateway. Look at the application and service log for on premise data gateway services.

Path: Events>Application and services log>On-premises data gateway services

1. Error encountered trying to connect to the server- We reached the data gateway, but the gateway cannot access the on –premises data sources. Validate that the SQL server is running.

Reference Section 7.3 below for additional Data Gateway information.

#### Scenario 9: Data Loading Errors

AFLPA data errors are outlined in the AFLPA Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) that will be used by the BusOps operations staff. Errors received while processing correspondence letter packages will be initially addressed by the BusOps operations staff, as required they may engage BusOps technical support staff to assist in addressing AFLPA errors.

The AFLPA exceptions listed in the table below involve loading information and correspondence letters into the AFLPA database. If BusOps operations staff is notified of any of these exceptions, they should contact the appropriate BusOps technical support staff for exceptions of type ‘UE (Unexpected Exceptions)’ or open a ServiceNow ticket for exceptions of type ‘BD (Bad Data exceptions)

Bad Data Exceptions:

| BIC | CIN\_NULL | CIN cannot be null or empty. |
| BIC | CIN\_LT\_9 | CIN cannot be less than 9 characters. |
| BIC | STADDR2\_NULL | Street Address 2 cannot be null or empty. |
| BIC | CITY\_NULL | City cannot be null or empty. |
| BIC | ZIP\_NULL | ZIP5 cannot be null or empty. |
| BIC | ZIP\_NONNUMERIC | ZIP5 should be numeric. |
| BIC | ZIP\_LT\_5 | ZIP5 cannot be less than 5 characters. |
| BIC | ZIP4\_NONNUMERIC | ZIP4 should be numeric. |
| BIC | ZIP4\_LT\_4 | ZIP4 cannot be less than 4 characters. |
| BIC | BEN\_NAME\_NULL | Beneficiary Name cannot be null or empty. |
| BIC | ACCTNMBR\_NULL | Account Number cannot be null or empty in BIC Card 2 file |
| FAME | CIN\_NULL | CIN cannot be null or empty. |
| FAME | CIN\_LT\_9 | CIN cannot be less than 9 characters. |
| FAME | LAST\_NAME\_NULL | Last Name cannot be null or empty. |

| FAME | DOD\_INVALID\_DATE | Date of Death has invalid date value. |

#### Scenario 10: Print Center has an issue with or did not receive the BIC follow-up letter file sent from AFLPA

This problem can be detected by:

* Reviewing email notifications that identified errors or exceptions in the process of generating BIC follow-up letter files.
* Receiving a notification from the Print Center that there was an issue processing the BIC follow-up letter file sent by AFLPA.
* Reviewing the Print Center reporting spreadsheet (Medi-Cal (RCOC) Rancho Production Status Report) and seeing that the BIC follow-up letter count is zero indicating that no BIC follow-up letters were generated.

To solve this problem:

1. Verify with the Print Center if they received the BIC follow-up letter file for the day in question. If not, re-send the BIC follow-up letter file to the Print Center.
2. Verify that the BIC follow-up letter file was generated properly and that the file structure and layout is correct. If there is a problem with the BIC follow-up letter file, repair it and re-send the BIC follow-up letter file to the Print Center.
3. Verify the weekly BIC follow-up letter process ran successfully. If it did not, then re-run the weekly BIC follow-up letter process to generate the BIC follow-up letter file for the Print Center.

# AFLPA Web Application and System Backups

AFLPA will use existing tools for application and system backups within the ODC.

Backups are performed on the following cadence:

* Daily – Incremental
* Weekly Full
* Monthly Full

Backups are performed daily on a random schedule where one day of the week a full backup is accomplished and on the other six (6) days of the week a differential backup is accomplished. All backups are encrypted. Backups are initially sent to disk as per standard Gainwell ITO retention policy. Online backups are maintained in the ODC. The files backed up to tape are rotated to an offsite location so that the most current copy is offsite at Iron Mountain Services in Orlando, FL and a previous copy is returned or stored off-site for archiving. Both full and differential backups are maintained for 30-days.

Please refer to the AFLPA TRP for additional details.

## AFLPA System Backup

AFLPA systems will be backed up utilizing NetBackup capabilities in the ODC. NetBackup will execute daily incremental backups throughout the week and then a full backup will be executed on the weekend. Database servers require a NetBackup agent to be installed on the server to perform system and database backups. Non-Database servers do not require a NetBackup agent to be installed on the system but are backed up with NetBackup by using system snapshots. If specific files must be restored or retrieved from a backup, this will be done through the NetBackup agent. Therefore, any specific files being restored or retrieved from NetBackup will be copied to a AFLPA system with a NetBackup agent and then moved to the appropriate destination AFLPA system

The AFLS file must be loaded after the latest update to the FAME file otherwise thousands of records will not load properly because the corresponding CIN has not been loaded into the database. As a result, the AFLS file will be transferred on Saturdays after the latest update for the FAME file. The FAME file or files will be processed and loaded to the AFLPA database first and then the AFLS file will be loaded to prevent thousands of AFLS records receiving exceptions because the CIN is not found in the AFLPA database.

## BIC Card Database Loads

AFLPA will receive the BIC Card 1 and BIC Card 2 files each business day as input files via MFT MOVEit jobs. An AFLPA process will parse the BIC Card files and load BIC card records into the AFLPA database. Each day an AFLPA process will delete BIC card records from the AFLPA database if they are older than 30 calendar days.

If there are errors or exceptions during the BIC card database load process, the error or exception will be logged, and a notification sent in an email.

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_AFLPA_Appendix_P_Runbooks.md#bic-follow-up-letter-database-loads]

## BIC Follow-Up Letter Database Loads

Weekly after the processing of the AFLS file, an AFLPA process will query the BIC card records in the database and determine if any recipients of BIC cards have selected an alternative format for their correspondence preference. If BIC card records are found, then a BIC follow-up letter job is created to send a BIC follow-up letter to the beneficiary in their selected alternative format. If a BIC follow-up letter has been sent, then it is flagged in the BIC card database information so that multiple letters are not sent out during the 30 calendar days that the BIC card records reside in the AFLPA database.

If there are errors or exceptions during the BIC follow-up letter process, the error or exception will be logged, and a notification sent in an email.

# Input Data File Retention

The AFLPA receives multiple input files for correspondence letter packages. These input files are retained as an archive file for seven (7) calendar days to make sure that all required input file elements were successfully loaded into AFLPA. After seven (7) calendar days the archive files are deleted from the application server using a power shell script. The power shell script scans through the archive folders and purges any files that are 7 days old.

BIC card data is held in the AFLPA database for 30 calendar days to allow for generating BIC Follow-up letters. Once BIC card data exceeds 30 calendar days it is deleted from the database. The data is dropped using SSIS package.

The AFLS file is received weekly and retained in the archive folder for even (7) calendar days to ensure that all required input file elements were successfully loaded into AFLPA. After seven (7) calendar days the archive files are deleted from the application server using a power shell script.

The FAME file is received daily and retained in the archive folder for even (7) calendar days to ensure that all required input file elements were successfully loaded into AFLPA. After seven (7) calendar days the archive files are deleted from the application server using a power shell script.

Mainframe, SURGE and CRM source files are received as generated by the source systems and retained in the AFLPA archive folder for even (7) calendar days to ensure that all required input file elements were successfully loaded into AFLPA. After seven (7) calendar days the archive files are deleted from the application server using a power shell script.
